carmen_a: alert from audit-bot: sudden spike in KMS 403s from onprem-priv cluster during tonight's hardening window :warning:
lee_ops: saw it. rollouts: host-egress-lockdown + rbac-tighten applied at 02:50 UTC (commit fe12b3). KMS endpoint is customer-managed at 10.9.3.7:443.
tara_sec: important to separate the two hypotheses: 1) netpol/host egress blocking connections; 2) RBAC token scope change causing AccessDenied. which one aligns with timeline?
audit-bot: KMS audit snippet (sanitized):
```
2026-03-23T02:53:05Z KMS AUTH FAIL svcacct:svc-keystore scope=decrypt status=403 reason=Forbidden
2026-03-23T02:53:12Z KMS AUTH FAIL svcacct:svc-keystore scope=decrypt status=403 reason=Forbidden
2026-03-23T02:54:00Z KMS CONNECT TIMEOUT from 10.23.4.12: ephemeral conn reset
```
lee_ops: node-level logs show iptables policy reloaded at 02:51 with DROP default for egress on eth0, plus a host-level conntrack prune cron that ran at 02:52.
lee_ops: running `ss -tnp` on affected host now; will paste trimmed output.
infra-bot: note: no IAM policy changes detected in cloud audit trail between 02:40-03:00.
lee_ops: ss output: many sockets in SYN_SENT to 10.9.3.7 and then RST from local firewall. looks like network blocked.
tara_sec: good. still capture assertion: why 403 rather than just timeout? if connection reset early, some requests may reach KMS but fail auth due to truncated TLS handshake or missing headers. also KMS can return 403 if token presented lacks required scope. we need to confirm token was not rotated.
carmen_a: timeline: 02:45 start hardening (canary), 02:50 global push, 02:53 audit alerts. we saw 4 failed decrypts from svc-keystore within 90s.
lee_ops: mitigation: temporarily relax host egress for keystore pods to allow 10.9.3.7/32:443; applied at 02:58. immediate success: decrypts return 200.
audit-bot: incident created: INC-2026-043 severity=high owner=lee_ops.
tara_sec: next steps: 1) preserve host netfilter rules and conntrack state for forensics (lee_ops). 2) snapshot KMS audit logs (carmen). 3) capture kube-apiserver audit slice for RBAC changes (tara). 4) check CI pipeline for RBAC role binding modify at ~02:40-02:55 (infra-bot).
infra-bot: CI: one pipeline job ran (infra/egress-hardening) at 02:48, and another (rbac-minimize) at 02:49. both triggered by same deploy batch fe12b3.
lee_ops: running forensic capture: /var/log/conntrack-snips and iptables-save copied to s3://sec-forensics/INC-5378911111.
carmen_a: KMS audit shows token issuer = internal-token-service v1, token exp 2026-03-23T03:30Z, same token used across requests; no sign of immediate token rotation.
tara_sec: we should treat as rollout regression. two overlapping changes (egress + rbac) in same batch -> blameworthy combination. action: split netpol and RBAC changes going forward. add smoke test: simple decrypt via staging KMS target from each canary node before wider rollout.
lee_ops: agreed. I'll add a preflight hook to helm job that runs `kubectl exec` into keystore pod and performs a decrypt against a staging key, with timeout 10s. if it fails, abort.
infra-bot: creating PR template update: require "keystore e2e decrypt" check for all egress/rbac rollouts.
tara_sec: also schedule a short rotation for the svc-keystore token if audit shows reuse across unexpected origins. for now we haven't seen anomalous issuers.
carmen_a: post-incident checklist: update runbook to include conntrack prune timing and host iptables reload safety net; define who hits rollback.
lee_ops: retrospective owner = lee_ops, security follow-up = tara_sec. timeline and RCA due by EOD tomorrow. thanks team :white_check_mark:
audit-bot: INC-2026-043 status=mitigated timestamp=5378911195
